To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of high-performance concrete (HPC) with large aggregates and steel fibres in the first layer and a conventional concrete (CC) with small aggregates in the second layer is the best way to engineer a layered barrier for impact resistance.
the resistance of high-performance concrete (HPC) to impact of non- deforming projectiles is affected by: (a) the type and the size of the aggregate; (b) the application of fibres.

(1) The impact resistance of high-strength concrete is affected by the aggregate size and type, and by the application of steel fibre reinforcement; (2) A layered barrier may be designed to utilize these effects to achieve an enhanced performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high-performance concrete for the construction of protective barriers.
the effects of high performance concrete mix ingredients on the resistance of single and layered protective barriers.
the development of high-performance concrete (HPC), which can be used to engineer protective barriers that resist the impact of high-velocity non-deforming projectiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a layered barrier may be designed and engineered for high-performance concrete based on the effects of the ingredients on the impact resistance.
the use of large aggregate sizes in front layers and steel fibres in the rear layers of protective barriers would lead to a better resistance to impact of high-performance concrete.
high-performance concrete mix design is important in the engineering of protective barriers, but it is not a panacea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a combination of the aggregate types (i.e. large and small) and the application of fibres in a layered barrier can produce better resistance to impact than the use of a single aggregate type.

the use of high performance concrete for protective barriers can be engineered to provide a better performance under projectile impacts, and the application of a thick, high-performance front layer and a thinner rear layer, which is made with normal strength concrete, is a good engineering approach.
the high-performance concrete mix design is an effective approach to enhance the resistance of protective barriers against impact of non-deformable projectiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resistance of high-performance concrete (HPC) barriers can be improved by the application of steel fibers and the use of large-sized aggregates in the outer, front layer.
high-performance concrete (HPC) mix design can be optimized to improve its ballistic resistance.
the use of high-performance concrete (HPC) can be an effective way of engineering protective barriers to be more resistant to the impact of non-deformable projectiles.
